title: Ops signal flow and customer bulletins
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for how SRE runs signal flow during an active incident and drafts customer-visible bulletins. Focus: simple, repeatable, low-friction templates that an on-call engineer + comms lead can use without customization.

Scope:
- Status page short messages and extended updates
- Customer-facing email/CS-facing bulletin templates by SLA tier
- Internal war-room checklist and role assignments
- Quick decision heuristics (when to escalate to exec comms, when to issue credit)

NOTE: Very much a draft. Use in conjunction with the master incident lifecycle page (linked above).

----
War-room quick checklist (first 10 minutes)
- Join #incidents immediately and create thread with timestamped title: [INCIDENT] <service> degraded (start: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC)
- Create war-room Google doc in the incidents folder and paste an initial summary. Tag on-call, tech lead, SRE manager.
- Assign roles (minimum):
  - Incident Lead / Decision Maker: owns status cadence and public comms
  - Tech Lead: drives investigation and mitigation plan
  - Communications Lead: writes status updates and liaises with CS/Support
  - Triage/Runbook operator: performs initial checks and runs diagnostic playbooks
  - Customer Liaison (optional): contacts top-tier customers if impacted
- Set cadence: 15m updates for sev1, 30m for sev2 unless otherwise agreed.
- Post initial status to status.redwood.ai and pin the post in #incidents.

Signal flow rules (who posts what where)
- On-call (Tech Lead) posts technical markers to war-room doc and to #incidents thread: short bullet of observed symptoms + ETA for next update.
- Communications Lead converts latest technical bullet into: one-line status page short status, and an internal Slack update summary for CS.
- Customer Liaison escalates to CS teams and triggers customer-specific messages for P1/P0 impacted customers.

Severity mapping (quick):
- P0 / Sev1: platform-wide outage or sustained >50% degraded requests >5 minutes. Immediate exec comms.
- P1 / Sev2: critical feature degraded for many customers or severe performance regressions for paid tiers. Internal comms + customer bulletins for impacted accounts.
- P2 / Sev3: localized problem, single-region impact, or small set of customers. Triage + postmortem.

Status page templates (short)
- Template A (outage):
  Short: "Investigating — We are aware of an issue affecting <service>. Users may see errors or failed requests. Our engineers are investigating."
  Updated fields: incident id, impacted regions, start time, next update ETA
- Template B (degraded performance):
  Short: "Degraded performance — Some users may experience slow response times for <service>. We are assessing scope and will provide updates."
- Template C (resolved):
  Short: "Resolved — The issue affecting <service> has been resolved. If you continue to see problems, please contact support."

Status page extended update (example)\- For the status page long body and email bullets, include these parts:
  1) Summary: short one-line statement (what happened)
  2) Scope: impacted customers, regions, features, and percentage estimate if known
  3) Timeline: what changed and when (bullet list with timestamps)
  4) Mitigation: actions taken so far and current mitigation state
  5) Next steps: what we're doing and ETA for next update
  6) Customer guidance: recommended workarounds or retries
  7) Contact: support channels and escalation path for paying customers

Example extended status (copy/paste editable):
- Title: Ongoing disruption to Redwood API text-generation (INC-2025-042)
- Summary: We are investigating elevated error rates for the Redwood text-generation API that began at 2025-05-11T14:03Z. Some requests are returning 5xx errors or timing out.
- Scope: A subset of requests routed to region us-west-2 and to model variant gpt-large-quant appear impacted. Estimated 12% of requests at the peak.
- Timeline:
  - 14:03 UTC — Alerts triggered for increased 5xx rates
  - 14:07 UTC — On-call acknowledged and opened war-room
  - 14:20 UTC — Rolling back recent deployment (v1.4.2 -> v1.4.1) as mitigation
- Mitigation: rollback completed 14:25 UTC; error rates reduced but intermittent failures persist. Autoscaling increased pool capacity to compensate.
- Next steps: engineering investigating root cause of increased latency in the KV cache layer; next update in 15 minutes.
- Customer guidance: retry requests, prefer smaller sequence lengths when possible; contact support with request ids.

Customer bulletin matrix (who to notify and how)
- Tier: Enterprise (contracted) -> Notification: direct email + Slack + status page; Owner: Customer Liaison + AM
- Tier: Paid (dedicated/dedicated-lite) -> Notification: email to billing admins + status page; Owner: CS Ops
- Tier: Free / Self-serve -> Notification: status page + in-product banner (if available)

Customer email template — enterprise (short):
Subject: Incident: Redwood API degradation impacting text-generation (ongoing)\\n
Hi <Customer-Contact-Name>,\\n\\nWe wanted to let you know we are currently investigating an issue impacting text-generation requests routed to us-west-2. You may see failed requests or increased latency. Our engineers have identified a candidate mitigation and are rolling it out; we will follow up with an ETA and next steps in the next 30 minutes.\\n\\nIf this is causing a production outage for you, please reply or escalate to your AM and we will prioritize.\\n\\n— Asha (on-call, Redwood SRE)\\n
Customer email template — general (short):
Subject: Redwood status update: service degradation

We are aware of an issue affecting <service>. We are investigating and will post updates to our status page: https://status.redwood.ai.

(Include contact instructions for paid customers)

Internal Slack update template (for #incidents thread):
- [HH:MM UTC] SHORT: Elevated 5xx for text-gen (us-west-2), suspected regression post-deploy v1.4.2. On-call running rollback. Next update +15m.

Guidelines for public phrasing (dos/don'ts):
- DO: Be transparent about impact and ETA. Say what we know, and what we don't.
- DO: Use non-technical language for customer emails; avoid internal jargon.
- DON'T: Speculate about root cause in early updates. Avoid naming unconfirmed third-party failures.

Escalation decision tree (simple):
- If >50% error rate for >5 minutes => escalate to SRE manager and exec comms (page on-call manager).
- If a single customer is experiencing a production outage => involve Customer Liaison and AM, consider targeted mitigation and follow-up call.

Post-incident checklist (first 24h)
- Confirm status: mark incident resolved on status page once verified.
- Immediate customer follow-up: send targeted emails to impacted customers with summary and next steps.
- Data collection: collect logs, request ids, and timeline for postmortem.
- Postmortem owner assigned within 48 hours. Draft due in 7 days.

Open questions & notes (to resolve in next edition)
- Decide: standard cadence for 3rd-party provider mentions — present policy is conservative but ambiguous.
- Add: Short template for in-product banner copy (needs product input).
- Confirm: which AMs should be auto-subscribed to incident emails for Enterprise tier (currently manual).

References and quick links
- War-room template (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/INCIDENTS
- Postmortem template: CONFLUENCE: Postmortem-Template-2024
- Monitoring dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts

Notes to self (working bullets)
- This needs to be trimmed to two 4-line templates for comms interns to use.
- Keep customer-facing language consistent across teams; coordinate with product-marketing for wording.
- Consider automating the short status page post from the metrics alert (safe defaults only).

Revision history:
- 2024-11-02 — initial draft by Asha Patel
- 2025-02-10 — added customer matrix, severity heuristics (Liam Chen)
- 2025-06-12 — updated example extended status and post-incident timings (Rosa Martinez)

END OF DOCUMENT
